notes: ROBOTS.TXT: checked both www.made.com/robots.txt and www.nextdirect.com/robots.txt for a Claude-specific disallow (ClaudeBot, anthropic-ai, Claude-Web) before any WAF-bypass attempt - neither present; no bypass restriction applies here.  RULE 3 / SITE IDENTITY: made.com/nl/ is NOT a live Made.com catalogue. It is a chain of three 301 redirects, fully confirmed via curl_cffi (safari15_3) with allow_redirects and history capture: https://www.made.com/nl/ -> 301 -> https://www.nextdirect.com/nl/nl/made -> 301 -> https://www.nextdirect.com/nl/nl/shop/brand-madecom -> 301 -> https://www.nextdirect.com/nl/nl/brands/madecom (200, final). This is a materially DIFFERENT and MORE DIMINISHED situation than S.N. 51 Made.com UK (read first, per assignment): UK stayed on the made.com domain and runs its own Next-operated storefront with real department URLs (/shop/lighting, /shop/tableware, etc, 1758 products total). NL leaves the made.com domain entirely and lands on nextdirect.com - Next's general international multi-category retail site (clothing, homeware, everything) - where 'Made' exists only as a BRAND FILTER FACET (brand:madecom) inside Next's broader Homeware department, not as any kind of dedicated storefront or category tree. Page <title> is literally 'MADE | Next Official Site', meta description 'Shop for MADE at Next.' SITE LEGITIMACY: nextdirect.com is genuinely Next's own platform (image assets served from cms.platform.next, the same Next CMS infrastructure identified at made.com UK); no closing-down-sale language, no scam indicators - this is Next Retail's real international storefront, just with Made reduced to a brand tag. CATALOGUE SIZE: the entire brand:madecom facet totals only 94 products SITE-WIDE (all under the single department:homeware facet value - no lighting, no furniture-as-separate-dept even appears), independently confirmed via the embedded search JSON (search.totalResults:94) and via the facets.department:homeware.c:94 count on https://www.nextdirect.com/nl/nl/brands/madecom. Of those 94, the category facet breaks out as: cushions 25, bedsets 20, dinnerware 8, curtains 7, wallart 5, glasses 4, towels 4, vases 4, pillowcases 4, throws 3, bedsheets 2, bathmats 2, bowls 2, plantpots 1 (facet counts do not sum to 94 exactly because some products carry no category tag or multiple tags - a facet-list artifact, not a count error). CRITICALLY: no Lighting category, no Mirrors category and no Clocks category exist anywhere in this brand facet (Made UK by contrast had 396 Lighting rows + 32 Mirrors + 7 Clocks) - confirming this is not a genuinely separate Dutch catalogue but a residual, near-liquidation-scale tail of Made SKUs folded into Next's general range.  ACCESS ROUTE: direct fetch and default-profile curl both hit Akamai 403 past the first redirect hop (chrome110/116/119/120/123/124/131 all 403 on nextdirect.com); curl_cffi impersonate=safari15_3 succeeded (HTTP 200) and was used for every page in this extraction. No proxy, no translate.goog, no browser automation needed.  COUNT METHOD: qty is the page's own embedded search JSON search.totalResults for each brand+category filtered URL (e.g. https://www.nextdirect.com/nl/nl/brands/madecom/f/category-glasses), INDEPENDENTLY PROVEN by exhaustion on unique structured product IDs (summaryData.id) - unique-ID count equalled totalResults on all 6 extracted categories (dinnerware 8=8, wallart 5=5, glasses 4=4, vases 4=4, bowls 2=2, plantpots 1=1); each count is small enough that a single page load is already a complete enumeration (all results render on one page, no pagination needed for n<=8). Glasses re-read twice (first pass + independent second fetch) and stayed stable at 4 both times; no drift observed on any of the 6 categories.  WHAT WAS EXTRACTED (Kitchen & Dining / Wall Decor & Mirrors / Home Accessories rules from the brief applied identically to UK): Dinnerware (8) - 'Millo 12 Piece Dinner Set', 'Quell' plate/bowl sets, tabletop dinnerware, kept under Kitchen & Dining. Glasses (4) - 'Cally Wine Glasses', 'Velma Crystal Cocktail Glasses', 'Theon Tumbler Glasses', kept under Kitchen & Dining per the ALL-glassware rule. Bowls (2) - 'Alysa Swirl Fruit Bowl', 'Maleah Fruit Bowl' - the SAME two fruit-bowl products already recorded in c51.json's UK Bowls row, evidencing this is the same underlying Made product catalogue distributed EUR-priced to NL via Next's platform, kept under Kitchen & Dining. Wall Art (5) - 'Alonzo Embroidered Wall Art', 'Ronja Wall Art', 'Dixie Sculptural Wall Art', 'Caito Wall Art', 'Abstract Canvas Wall Art', kept under Wall Decor & Mirrors as a single leaf (only one sub-category exists in this bucket, no further children, so no parent row per the brief's single-leaf exception). Vases (4) - 'Mira Glass Vase' x2 colourways, 'Kian Hand Painted Vase', 'Juro Stainless Steel Vase', kept under Home Accessories. Plant Pots (1) - 'Piper Plant Pot', kept under Home Accessories as decorative planter, same product line as c51's UK Plant Pots row.  EXCLUDED AND WHY (product titles read in every case): Cushions (25) and Throws (3) and Pillowcases (4) - soft furnishings/textiles, excluded. Bedsets (20) and Bedsheets (2) - bedding, excluded. Curtains (7) - textile window coverings, excluded. Towels (4) - bath textiles, excluded. Bathmats (2) - 'Etly Stripe 100% Cotton Bath Mat', bathroom textile/utility not decor, excluded (Rule 0.4 still excludes bathroom textiles/hardware; only bathroom mirrors/lighting are protected, and neither category exists in this facet). No Lighting, Mirrors, Clocks or Candle Holders categories exist in the brand:madecom facet at all - nothing to apply Rule 0 to; there is no room-based branch present to test against Rule 0 either, unlike UK's Lighting-by-Room branch, because Lighting itself is entirely absent from this facet. No home-fragrance, artificial-plant, or holiday nodes present.  CURRENCY/LOCALE: confirmed genuinely NL-served (siteCountry:NL, siteLanguage:nl, currencyCode:EUR, og:locale nl_NL, Dutch facet labels e.g. 'Kussentjes'=cushions, 'Vazen'=vases, 'Schalen'=bowls), not a raw UK mirror, though it draws from the same product catalogue as UK per the identical Bowls/Plant-Pot SKUs noted above.
